Baram v0.7.3 is a repair release. Every change below exists because a document did not
come back the way it was written, or because the editor stopped responding to one.

## Your document comes back as you wrote it

Baram's first promise is that a file survives the trip into the editor and out again.
Four separate ways it did not are fixed here.

- **Table cells were padded out with spaces on save.** The writer aligned every cell to
  the width of its column, so opening a table and saving rewrote rows you never touched
  and buried the real edit in a diff of whitespace.
- **Inline code swallowed the formatting around it.** A span that was both code and bold,
  or code inside a link, was written back as plain code — the other marks were dropped on
  the way out and could not come back.
- **A custom mark wrapping another mark lost it silently.** `^**bold**^`, `==*text*==`
  and their relatives were written in a form the reader could not parse back, so the
  inner marks disappeared on reload. This one was the worst of the four to notice,
  because the bytes on disk could be unchanged — the file looked fine and the document
  did not.
- **Moving the pointer across a table marked its columns resized.** The resize tracker
  fired on the plugin metadata Prosemirror dispatches for every mouse move over a table,
  not just for a finished drag, and it marked every table in the document rather than the
  one under the cursor. Opening one real file and moving the mouse across it turned
  25,095 bytes into 43,158, full of `<!-- colwidths:... -->` comments nobody asked for. A
  width is now recorded only when a drag actually ends, and only for the table it ended
  in.

## A table with 50 rows no longer freezes the app

Tables above roughly fifty rows could lock the window permanently — not slow, stopped.
The cause was a virtual-scrolling plugin that never worked in the first place: it drove
rendering with `content-visibility` on `<tr>` elements, where the CSS specification makes
the property have no effect at all. It bought nothing and cost everything, so it is gone.
Tables render all of their rows.

If you have seen "tables support virtual scrolling" in the README, that line was
describing a feature that never shipped. It has been removed.

## Exports read more of your note, and admit what they could not read

Pandoc exports (Word, EPUB, LaTeX, RST) keep the image policy introduced in v0.7.2 and
widen what it can carry.

- **An `<img>` tag you wrote by hand is now embedded**, not just one Baram wrote when you
  resized an image — as long as the HTML around it is only tags, comments and caption
  text. Pandoc keeps parsing Markdown inside an HTML block, so a tag sitting next to a
  code fence, a backtick, a `$`, a bracket, a pipe table or a four-space indent is code,
  math or link data to Pandoc rather than an image. A fragment like that is left exactly
  as written, and the notice tells you images in it may be missing.
- **One export embeds at most 256 images**, and the notice says how many went past the
  limit and became alt text.
- **An `<img>` with no source gets counted and explained on its own**, instead of being
  folded into the count of images that were dropped for their path.
- **You are warned before an embedding export when no open vault or folder contains the
  note.** Relative paths have nothing to resolve against in that case, so every relative
  image would have degraded to alt text after the export finished. Now you hear it first.

## Also fixed

- **HTML blocks kept their images pointed at the previous file's folder.** The block
  re-resolved relative media paths only as a side effect of React reassigning its markup
  on every render. React 19.3 compares the markup string and skips that reassignment, so
  after a tab switch the images stayed resolved against the old directory. The block now
  performs that reset itself rather than relying on a framework detail.

---

**Updating.** Every platform installs in place and restarts — press **Install & Restart**
in the update dialog. Linux `.deb` and `.rpm` cannot be updated in place by the updater;
those, and any install that fails, open the releases page instead.
